svg.text: Interactive biology lesson · drag each label onto its matching part of the flower
Drag each label tile from the word bank onto the matching
empty slot on the flower diagram. Use the buttons below if
1. Read the slot number near each arrow on the flower.
2. Pick the matching label from the word bank below.
3. Drop it onto the corresponding slot.
4. Press Check Answer to see how you did.
How pollen travels from anther to stigma
A bee carries pollen from Flower A’s anther to Flower B’s stigma.

g.text: Tip: A stamen = anther + filament. A pistil = stigma + style + ovary.
Compare your placements with the correct answers below.
Colourful leaf-like structure that attracts pollinators.
Sticky top of the pistil that catches pollen.
Yellow tip of stamen that produces pollen.
Small green leaf protecting the flower bud.
Swollen tip of stem where flower parts attach.
All dropped labels will return to the word bank, and every slot on the
flower diagram will be cleared. Your progress will reset to 0 / 10.
Click anywhere on the dim background or the X button to dismiss this panel.
